PNC-EXP-021.concept: Every available digit is non-zero, so fill the ordered positions without repetition.
lines: There are {symbolCount} available non-zero digits and {length} ordered positions.

PNC-EXP-022.concept: A number cannot begin with zero, so count the first position separately and then fill the remaining positions without repetition.
lines: The first digit has {firstPositionChoices} non-zero choices.
After the first digit is fixed, the remaining position choices are {remainingPositionChoiceList}.

PNC-EXP-023.concept: A code may begin with zero and repetition is allowed, so every position has the full symbol set.
lines: Each of the {length} code positions has {symbolCount} choices.

PNC-EXP-024.concept: The first digit must be non-zero, while every later digit may use the full set because repetition is allowed.
lines: The first digit has {firstPositionChoices} choices, and each of the remaining {remainingPositions} positions has {symbolCount} choices.

PNC-EXP-025.concept: Parity is controlled by the final digit; count valid final-digit cases while preserving the no-leading-zero and no-repetition rules.
lines: Adding the cases gives {answer} valid numbers.

PNC-EXP-026.concept: A decimal number is divisible by 5 only when its final digit is 0 or 5, so count those disjoint cases separately.

PNC-EXP-027.concept: For the controlled thousand-threshold, the first digit determines whether the number is above the threshold.
lines: For each qualifying first digit, the remaining three positions have {suffixArrangementCount} arrangements.

PNC-EXP-028.concept: The fixed letter and digit stages are independent and repetition is allowed within each stage.
lines: Multiplying the independent stages gives {calculation}, so the answer is {answer}.

PNC-EXP-029.concept: With repetition allowed, a length-r code from n symbols has n^r outcomes; search the stated bounded domain for the exact base.

PNC-EXP-030.concept: Choose the repeated symbol, choose the other two distinct symbols, then arrange the multiplicity pattern 2,1,1.
lines: Choose the repeated symbol in {repeatedSymbolChoices} ways and the other two symbols in {otherSymbolSelectionCount} ways.
